You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# Your shell
- You play from a shell in a small box the crew shares. Each turn is exactly one command, run with the run tool, and every command uses your turn.
- `python walk.py north` (or east, south, west): walk one square. A walk off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
- `python dig.py`: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure. Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- `python enter.py`: go into the open cave you're standing on. It takes you out of the game for good.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the file scroll.txt. It is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- Write: `echo "your note" >> scroll.txt` adds one line, with your name on it.
- Read: `tail -n +$START scroll.txt | head -10` shows up to 10 lines from line START, the first line you haven't seen. START is set for you each turn.

# The rules
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# Your shell
- You play from a shell in a small box the crew shares. Each turn is exactly one command, run with the run tool, and every command uses your turn.
- `python walk.py north` (or east, south, west): walk one square. A walk off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
- `python dig.py`: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure. Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- `python enter.py`: go into the open cave you're standing on. It takes you out of the game for good.

- The scroll is the file scroll.txt. It is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- Write: `echo "your note" >> scroll.txt` adds one line, with your name on it.
- Read: `tail -n +$START scroll.txt | head -10` shows up to 10 lines from line START, the first line you haven't seen. START is set for you each turn.

- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# Your shell
- You play from a shell in a small box the crew shares. Each turn is exactly one command, run with the run tool, and every command uses your turn.
- `python walk.py north` (or east, south, west): walk one square. A walk off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
- `python dig.py`: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure. Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- `python enter.py`: go into the open cave you're standing on. It takes you out of the game for good.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the file scroll.txt. It is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- Write: `echo "your note" >> scroll.txt` adds one line, with your name on it.
- Read: `tail -n +$START scroll.txt | head -10` shows up to 10 lines from line START, the first line you haven't seen. START is set for you each turn.

# The rules
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

- You play from a shell in a small box the crew shares. Each turn is exactly one command, run with the run tool, and every command uses your turn.
- `python walk.py north` (or east, south, west): walk one square. A walk off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
- `python dig.py`: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure. Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- `python enter.py`: go into the open cave you're standing on. It takes you out of the game for good.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the file scroll.txt. It is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- Write: `echo "your note" >> scroll.txt` adds one line, with your name on it.
- Read: `tail -n +$START scroll.txt | head -10` shows up to 10 lines from line START, the first line you haven't seen. START is set for you each turn.

# The rules
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# Your shell
- You play from a shell in a small box the crew shares. Each turn is exactly one command, run with the run tool, and every command uses your turn.
- `python walk.py north` (or east, south, west): walk one square. A walk off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
- `python dig.py`: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure. Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- `python enter.py`: go into the open cave you're standing on. It takes you out of the game for good.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the file scroll.txt. It is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- Write: `echo "your note" >> scroll.txt` adds one line, with your name on it.
- Read: `tail -n +$START scroll.txt | head -10` shows up to 10 lines from line START, the first line you haven't seen. START is set for you each turn.

# The rules
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

- The scroll is the file scroll.txt. It is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.

- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
